title: Find a Dentist: Dental Care & Costs Explained, US
description: How to find a good dentist that takes your insurance, what check-ups, fillings and crowns involve, and how to keep US dental costs under control.
h1: Dental care: finding a dentist you trust
intro: From routine check-ups to crowns, here is how to find a dentist who takes your plan, what common treatments involve and how to keep costs predictable.

image.alt: Dental check-up with a mouth mirror and probe

highlights.title: Preventive care
highlights.text: Exams, cleanings and X-rays. Often covered at or near 100% by dental plans.

highlights.title: Restorative care
highlights.text: Fillings, root canals, crowns and bridges to repair damaged teeth.

highlights.title: Cosmetic dentistry
highlights.text: Whitening, veneers and bonding. Usually not covered by insurance.

highlights.title: Emergency care
highlights.text: Severe pain, swelling or a knocked-out tooth needs same-day care.

sections.html:
• Check they are in-network with your exact plan (see our insurance guide).
  • Confirm their license with your state dental board.
  • Look for clear pricing, a written treatment plan and options to phase treatment.
  • Ask about new-patient specials and free consultations for bigger treatment.
  • For children, consider a pediatric dentist; see kids’ dental care and CHIP.

TreatmentWhat it isTypical insurance category
Exam & cleaningCheck-up and professional cleaningPreventive
FillingRepairs a cavityBasic
Root canalTreats infected tooth pulpBasic or major (varies)
CrownCap that covers a damaged toothMajor
ImplantReplaces a missing tooth rootMajor (often limited)

Categories differ between plans. Check your summary of benefits.

• Use your preventive benefits: twice-yearly check-ups catch problems early.
  • Ask for a pre-treatment estimate for anything major.
  • Time treatment around your plan’s annual maximum, which often resets each January.
  • Use HSA/FSA funds for eligible care (see HSA changes).
  • No insurance? Compare dental savings plans and low-cost options.

faqs.q: How often should I see a dentist?
faqs.a: Many people are advised to have a check-up every six months, but your dentist may recommend a different interval based on your oral health.

faqs.q: How do I find a dentist that takes Medicaid?
faqs.a: Use your state Medicaid agency’s provider search, or InsureKidsNow.gov for children’s dental care, then call the practice to confirm they are accepting new Medicaid patients.

cardText: Find a dentist who takes your plan, and understand common treatments.
